result.title: SLIM: Simplex-Lattice Interpolation Merging
result.summary: Optimizing merging coefficients for large language models can require many costly benchmark evaluations. We propose \textbf{Simplex-Lattice Interpolation Merging (SLIM)}, which constructs a quadratic surrogate of aggregate performance on the coefficient simplex using a classical mixture design. Evaluations of individual experts and equal-weight pairs determine the surrogate with the minimum number of measurements needed to identify a general quadratic on this domain. SLIM then optimizes the surrogate without further target-metric evaluations. Experiments on two model architectures demonstrate accurate prediction of unseen multi-expert mixtures and competitive merge performance under limited evaluation budgets. Matched-budget comparisons show that structured evaluation points improve prediction fidelity over random designs, including those using regularized fitting.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SLIM，用 simplex-lattice 混合实验设计构建聚合性能的二次代理模型，仅评估单个专家与等权配对即可预测未见多专家混合的效果，从而在有限评测预算下优化模型合并系数。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线的联系较弱，但其「少量结构化探测点拟合代理、再在代理上优化」的思路或可启发 latent 工作区的预测性评估与贡献分配，例如在不增加昂贵评测的前提下预测不同 latent 组合或推理深度配置的效用，需进一步核查其可迁移性。
